Tags: P is a primary source or an institution's own page, S is a secondary source such as a news report, magazine or data compilation. I read pages through a summarizing tool, so check figures against the original before citing.

p: The IPBES global assessment found that around 1 million animal and plant species are now threatened with extinction. It put the threatened share at more than 40 percent of amphibians, almost 33 percent of reef-forming corals and more than a third of marine mammals, with a tentative 10 percent for insects. The average abundance of native species in most major land-based habitats has fallen by at least 20 percent.
How solid A UN summary of the 2019 assessment. The insect figure is labelled tentative, and the page gives no share for all species.

kv.v: Ranked by global impact: changes in land and sea use, direct exploitation of organisms, climate change, pollution, and invasive alien species.

items.solid: How solid A UN summary of the 2019 assessment. The insect figure is labelled tentative, and the page gives no share for all species.

p: The IUCN Red List, in version 2023-1, puts the best-estimate threatened share at 41 percent of amphibians, 26 percent of mammals, 12 percent of birds, 36 percent of reef-forming corals, 70 percent of cycads and 34 percent of conifers. A magazine summary of the 2026 update reports 175,909 species on the list, of which 49,505 are threatened.
How solid The 2023 percentages come from the IUCN page, which gives ranges. The 2026 counts come from a magazine summary, not from IUCN, and I did not see the release date.

kv.v: Amphibians 36–47 percent, mammals 23–37, birds 12–13, reef corals 31–44, conifers 34–35.

items.solid: How solid The 2023 percentages come from the IUCN page, which gives ranges. The 2026 counts come from a magazine summary, not from IUCN, and I did not see the release date.

items.h3: Wildlife populations down 73 percent on average
p: The Living Planet Report 2026 tracks 35,803 populations of 5,790 species of mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians and fish. Their average decline was 73 percent from 1970 to 2022, about 2.5 percent a year.

How solid The report itself says the figure is not a headcount of animals lost and is especially sensitive to changes in already small populations. The 2026 edition added 295 species and 967 populations to the 2024 data.

kv.v: South America 95 percent, Africa 80 percent.
Freshwater 85 percent, land 69 percent, marine 59 percent.
Habitat loss and degradation were reported most often, followed by overexploitation, climate change, pollution, invasive species and disease.

items.solid: How solid The report itself says the figure is not a headcount of animals lost and is especially sensitive to changes in already small populations. The 2026 edition added 295 species and 967 populations to the 2024 data.

p: Our World in Data, summarizing a 2018 study in PNAS, gives humans 0.01 percent of total biomass and 2.5 percent of animal biomass. Livestock account for 4 percent of animal biomass, more than 50 percent above all humans together. Wild mammals and birds together account for 0.38 percent, so livestock outweigh them by a factor of ten.
How solid An estimate of mass, not of numbers. The page gives no figure for how much wild mammal biomass has changed over time, so it shows the present balance only.

kv.v: About 0.2 percent of animal biomass, more than twice that of wild birds.

items.solid: How solid An estimate of mass, not of numbers. The page gives no figure for how much wild mammal biomass has changed over time, so it shows the present balance only.

p: IPBES reports that 37,000 alien species have established worldwide and that 3,500 have become problematic invasives. The page says invasive alien species are the sole cause of 16 percent of extinctions and a major driver of 60 percent, and that they are responsible for 90 percent of extinctions on islands.
How solid Read through an Australian biodiversity council's summary of the report, not IPBES's own page. The page does not say whether the $423 billion is a yearly figure.

kv.v: A 2019 IPBES estimate of $423 billion. The cost of impacts has more than quadrupled every decade since 1970, according to the page.

items.solid: How solid Read through an Australian biodiversity council's summary of the report, not IPBES's own page. The page does not say whether the $423 billion is a yearly figure.

p: A 2017 study of flying insect biomass at 63 German nature reserves, measured from 1989, found an average fall of 76 percent over 27 years, and 82 percent in summer. A 2020 meta-analysis in Science of 166 long-term surveys at 1,676 sites worldwide, covering 1925 to 2018, found land insect abundance falling by an average of 0.92 percent a year, about 24 percent over 30 years.

How solid The 76 percent figure comes from a news report whose text gave no publication year (its web address is dated October 2017) and that says only that many reserves border farmland. The meta-analysis measures abundance, not species, and says local trends vary widely, with weaker trends in less disturbed areas described as tentative.

kv.v: The same meta-analysis found freshwater insect abundance rising by an average of 1.08 percent a year, about 38 percent over 30 years, which the authors link possibly to water protection policies.
Land declines were strongest in parts of the United States and in Europe, especially Germany, with the steepest European declines since 2005. Tree-canopy insects were largely unchanged.
The German study did not identify one; pesticides were a suggested explanation. The meta-analysis associates land declines with habitat destruction, particularly urbanization.

items.solid: How solid The 76 percent figure comes from a news report whose text gave no publication year (its web address is dated October 2017) and that says only that many reserves border farmland. The meta-analysis measures abundance, not species, and says local trends vary widely, with weaker trends in less disturbed areas described as tentative.

p: IPBES found that three-quarters of the land-based environment and about 66 percent of the marine environment have been significantly altered by human actions, and that land degradation has cut the productivity of 23 percent of the land surface. A UNCCD report, as covered by EcoWatch, says human activity has degraded as much as 40 percent of the world's land.

How solid The 23 percent and the up-to-40 percent use different definitions and sources, so they do not conflict. The UNCCD figures reached me through a news article, and the GDP claim is the article's.

kv.v: The UNCCD scenario calls for five billion hectares to be restored, which the article puts at 35 percent of Earth's land area.
The article says land degradation puts about half of global GDP at risk.

items.solid: How solid The 23 percent and the up-to-40 percent use different definitions and sources, so they do not conflict. The UNCCD figures reached me through a news article, and the GDP claim is the article's.

p: Global Forest Watch reports that the world lost 4.3 million hectares of tropical primary forest in 2025. That was 36 percent less than in 2024, and still 46 percent higher than a decade ago.
How solid WRI's own summary of Global Forest Watch data. The 42 percent fire share applies to all tree cover loss, not to tropical primary forest alone.

kv.v: Global tree cover loss was 25.5 million hectares in 2025, and fires caused 42 percent of it.

items.solid: How solid WRI's own summary of Global Forest Watch data. The 42 percent fire share applies to all tree cover loss, not to tropical primary forest alone.

p: FAO's 2015 Status of the World's Soil Resources reports that 33 percent of land is moderately to highly degraded through erosion, salinization, compaction, acidification and chemical pollution, and that conditions are worsening in far more cases than they are improving. Erosion removes 25 to 40 billion tonnes of topsoil each year.
How solid The FAO figures are from its own 2015 press release and are a decade old. The 59 percent is a synthesis of earlier estimates, not a census, and the page I read gives no margin of error.

kv.v: Cereal losses from erosion are estimated at 7.6 million tonnes a year, and could exceed 253 million tonnes by 2050 without action. Salinization affects an estimated 760,000 square kilometres.
A 2023 study led by Mark Anthony, in PNAS, estimates that 59 percent of all species depend on soil, including 90 percent of fungi, 86 percent of plants and 40 percent of bacteria.
FAO says the decline can be reversed if countries promote sustainable soil management.

items.solid: How solid The FAO figures are from its own 2015 press release and are a decade old. The 59 percent is a synthesis of earlier estimates, not a census, and the page I read gives no margin of error.

p: The Global Wetland Outlook 2025 reports a loss of more than 4 million square kilometres of wetland since 1970 across 11 wetland types, a 22 percent fall in extent. About a quarter of the remaining wetlands are degraded and are being destroyed at 0.52 percent a year.
How solid Read through a Mongabay summary. The value range is wide because the figure depends on how services are priced, and the forecast is the report's, not mine.

kv.v: Roughly 40 percent of the world's plant and animal species rely on wetlands at some point in their lives.
The remaining 14 million square kilometres provide $8 trillion to $39 trillion of ecosystem services a year.
Up to 20 percent of the world's wetlands could be lost in the next 25 years.

items.solid: How solid Read through a Mongabay summary. The value range is wide because the figure depends on how services are priced, and the forecast is the report's, not mine.

p: The FAO's State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2026 puts the share of sustainably fished stocks at 62.4 percent, which leaves 37.6 percent overfished. Wild catch was stable at about 92 million tonnes in 2024, inside the 86 to 94 million tonne band it has held since the late 1980s, while farmed aquatic animal production passed 100 million tonnes for the first time.
How solid Read through Mongabay. The number of assessed stocks rose from about 500 to 2,665, mostly because stocks were split into separate assessments, so comparison with earlier editions is harder.

kv.v: The sustainable share fell 2.1 points from the 2024 report.

items.solid: How solid Read through Mongabay. The number of assessed stocks rose from about 500 to 2,665, mostly because stocks were split into separate assessments, so comparison with earlier editions is harder.

p: NOAA confirmed the fourth global coral bleaching event on 15 April 2024. Bleaching-level heat stress ran from early 2023 to mid-2025 and reached 84 percent of the world's coral reef area. Mass bleaching was documented in at least 83 countries and territories across the Pacific, Atlantic and Indian oceans.

How solid NOAA's own page says the event likely concluded in mid-2025 and that it was waiting on the December 2025 to February 2026 summer to be sure; my read predates that check. The tipping-point statement comes from a Stockholm Resilience Centre summary that gives no temperature threshold.

kv.v: The 2025 Global Tipping Points report says warm-water coral reefs are now passing their tipping point, with widespread dieback under way. Reefs support nearly a billion people and a quarter of all marine life.

items.solid: How solid NOAA's own page says the event likely concluded in mid-2025 and that it was waiting on the December 2025 to February 2026 summer to be sure; my read predates that check. The tipping-point statement comes from a Stockholm Resilience Centre summary that gives no temperature threshold.

p: A magazine summary of the IUCN Red List 2026 update says about 62 percent of endemic hydrothermal vent molluscs, 125 of 201 species, are threatened by deep-sea mining. It names a deep-sea snail from the Indian Ocean, Lirapex felix, listed as Critically Endangered because of mining exploration.
How solid A secondary summary whose excerpt cut off, so other changes in the update may exist. No commercial mining has been approved; see the chapter on defenses.
items.solid: How solid A secondary summary whose excerpt cut off, so other changes in the update may exist. No commercial mining has been approved; see the chapter on defenses.

p: The World Glacier Monitoring Service reports net mass loss of 408 gigatonnes in the 2025 hydrological year for glaciers outside the ice sheets, sixth-most negative on record, equal to 1.1 millimetres of sea level. Since 1975 the cumulative loss is 9,583 gigatonnes, equal to 26.4 millimetres.
How solid WGMS's own report. Each figure carries an uncertainty (408 ± 132 Gt for 2025), and the page gives no share of ice lost.

kv.v: Annual loss rose from under 100 gigatonnes in 1976–1995 to about 230 in 1996–2015 and about 390 in 2016–2025.
Six of the highest mass-loss years on record fell in the past seven years.

items.solid: How solid WGMS's own report. Each figure carries an uncertainty (408 ± 132 Gt for 2025), and the page gives no share of ice lost.

p: NASA reports that average global sea level has risen about 10 centimetres since 1993, and that the annual rate of rise has more than doubled over three decades. In 2025 the rise was about 0.8 millimetres, down from about 5.9 millimetres in 2024.
How solid NASA's own page. The 2025 figure is one year and swings with ocean cycles such as La Niña; the trend over three decades is the point. I converted inches and centimetres to millimetres.
items.solid: How solid NASA's own page. The 2025 figure is one year and swings with ocean cycles such as La Niña; the trend over three decades is the point. I converted inches and centimetres to millimetres.

p: World plastic production rose nearly 230-fold, from 2 million tonnes in 1950 to 460 million tonnes in 2019. Roughly 350 million tonnes of plastic waste are generated each year, and about a quarter is mismanaged.
How solid Our World in Data's summary of OECD and academic estimates. The page says the uncertainties are large, and the ocean figure has been revised downward.

kv.v: Between 1 and 2 million tonnes a year are estimated to enter the oceans, about 0.5 percent of waste generated. Earlier estimates ran as high as 8 million.

items.solid: How solid Our World in Data's summary of OECD and academic estimates. The page says the uncertainties are large, and the ocean figure has been revised downward.

p: Our World in Data estimates that around half of the global population depends on synthetic nitrogen fertilizer, within a range of 40 to 50 percent. Without it the population may have been only about 4 billion, against over 8 billion in 2023.
How solid The fertilizer share is hard to derive with confidence, because breeding, irrigation and mechanization also raised yields.

kv.v: The 2026 Planetary Health Check lists modification of biogeochemical flows, which covers nitrogen, among the transgressed boundaries. The connection between the two entries is mine.

items.solid: How solid The fertilizer share is hard to derive with confidence, because breeding, irrigation and mechanization also raised yields.

p: The 2026 Planetary Health Check finds that seven of nine boundaries are transgressed: climate change, biosphere integrity, land system change, freshwater change, biogeochemical flows, novel entities and ocean acidification. All seven are at their highest recorded levels of transgression. Ocean acidification was the most recent to be breached, in 2025.
How solid Read through a summary posted on Astrobiology.com. The boundaries are a scientific framework, not a measured threshold at which collapse begins.

kv.v: Stratospheric ozone depletion and atmospheric aerosol loading, both improved over the last decade, though the authors caution that global progress may mask unsafe aerosol levels in some regions.

items.solid: How solid Read through a summary posted on Astrobiology.com. The boundaries are a scientific framework, not a measured threshold at which collapse begins.

p: Carbon dioxide at Mauna Loa rose from 313 parts per million in 1958 to a May 2026 peak of 432 parts per million. The WMO puts 2025 at 1.43 °C above the pre-industrial level, with an uncertainty of 0.13 °C.

How solid Both figures were read for the chapter on vulnerability, from a Japanese research-centre page citing the Mauna Loa record and from a trade-press report of the WMO statement. Neither is the original release.
items.solid: How solid Both figures were read for the chapter on vulnerability, from a Japanese research-centre page citing the Mauna Loa record and from a trade-press report of the WMO statement. Neither is the original release.

patterns.h3: Reach
p: Three-quarters of the land environment and two-thirds of the marine environment are significantly altered, and the 84 percent of reef area hit by heat stress shows that even remote ecosystems are affected.

patterns.h3: Scale
p: Plastic output grew about 230-fold from 1950 to 2019, carbon dioxide rose from 313 to 432 parts per million, and the yearly rate of glacier loss is roughly four times its 1976–1995 level.

patterns.h3: Speed
p: Monitored wildlife populations fell by an average of 73 percent in 52 years. The fourth global bleaching event reached 84 percent of reef area in about two and a half years.

patterns.h3: Dependence
p: Reefs support nearly a billion people, wetlands about 40 percent of species, and synthetic nitrogen about half of humanity, so pressure on these systems is linked to everything that depends on them.

patterns.h3: No clock for recovery
p: Several entries describe states, not flows: a reef tipping point said to be passing, seven boundaries at their highest recorded levels, and glaciers that lose ice faster each period.

limits: Measured records are short. The Living Planet index starts in 1970 and the satellite and bleaching records are far shorter, so the chapter cannot compare today with earlier centuries.
The measures are not comparable. The charts mix population indices, shares of area and shares of stocks, and the labels say which is which.
Indices have known weaknesses. The Living Planet figure is an average that is sensitive to small populations, and the Red List shares carry wide ranges.

Not covered: groundwater, air pollution's effect on ecosystems, noise, and the many local losses that never reach a global index. The insect and soil entries are thinner than the others, resting on few studies and, for soils, a 2015 report.
Most figures reached me through summaries, so they need checking against the original reports before use.

p: Two pulses of loss ended the Ordovician. One estimate puts the loss at 27 percent of families, 57 percent of genera and 85 percent of species.

How solid Contested. The figures depend on the method, the taxonomic unit and the correction for sampling bias, and the page says the Big Five are not sharply defined and sit in a continuum with many smaller events.

kv.v: The first pulse is linked to cooling and glaciation. A 2020 study instead favoured warming, volcanism and oxygen loss, which conflicts with earlier work. A later proposal links volcanic ash to carbon dioxide reduction, glaciation and anoxia.
Genus losses run from 42–46 percent in one estimate to 57 percent in another.

items.solid: How solid Contested. The figures depend on the method, the taxonomic unit and the correction for sampling bias, and the page says the Big Five are not sharply defined and sit in a continuum with many smaller events.

p: Two pulses, the Kellwasser and the Hangenberg, together removed about 19 percent of families, about 50 percent of genera and at least 70 percent of species.
How solid Contested. A supernova has been proposed for the Hangenberg pulse, which the page calls speculative, and the exact mechanisms remain debated.

kv.v: Oxygen-poor ocean events, possibly driven by volcanism, weathering by land plants and climate change. Kellwasser may have involved algal blooms fed by river nutrients.
Kellwasser genus loss ranges from 16–20 percent in one estimate to 40 percent in another.

items.solid: How solid Contested. A supernova has been proposed for the Hangenberg pulse, which the page calls speculative, and the exact mechanisms remain debated.

p: The greatest of the Big Five removed about 81 percent of marine species and about 70 percent of terrestrial vertebrate species. It was also the largest known extinction of insects. The main marine pulse fell within an interval of 60,000 to 100,000 years.

How solid Partly settled and partly not. Earlier marine estimates of 90–96 percent were later attributed to confusing this event with an earlier one, plant losses are disputed, and whether land and sea losses were simultaneous is contested.

kv.v: Flood basalt eruptions that formed the Siberian Traps released sulfur dioxide and carbon dioxide, leading to warming, acidified oceans and oxygen-starved, sulfurous seas. Carbon dioxide rose from about 400 to about 2,500 parts per million and temperatures by about 8 °C.
About 10 million years for most marine communities by some estimates, about 30 million for land vertebrates, and about 75 million for global marine diversity to regain its earlier level.

items.solid: How solid Partly settled and partly not. Earlier marine estimates of 90–96 percent were later attributed to confusing this event with an earlier one, plant losses are disputed, and whether land and sea losses were simultaneous is contested.

p: The event removed about 23 percent of families, 48 percent of genera and 70 to 75 percent of species. Marine genus loss is put at 55 percent.
How solid Estimates vary with the method: genus loss runs from 37 percent in one estimate to 73 percent in another.

kv.v: Volcanic activity, oxygen loss and warming. Falls in sea level are also associated with the event.

items.solid: How solid Estimates vary with the method: genus loss runs from 37 percent in one estimate to 73 percent in another.

p: About 75 percent of plant and animal species were lost. It is generally thought that an asteroid 10 to 15 kilometres wide struck the Yucatán Peninsula and caused a lingering impact winter, and a 2010 panel of 41 scientists endorsed that view.

How solid The asteroid is widely accepted as the cause, though whether it was the only one is disputed. Volcanism in the Deccan Traps, climate change and sea-level change are proposed as contributing factors.

kv.v: All non-avian dinosaurs, pterosaurs, mosasaurs, plesiosaurs and ammonites, about 60 percent of late-Cretaceous coral genera and about 98 percent of colonial coral species.
Birds, small mammals, more than 80 percent of turtle species and about half of crocodile-group species.
Forest plant diversity took about 6 million years to return, and lizards and snakes about 10 million.

items.solid: How solid The asteroid is widely accepted as the cause, though whether it was the only one is disputed. Volcanism in the Deccan Traps, climate change and sea-level change are proposed as contributing factors.

p: Global temperature rose by 5 to 8 °C in one estimate and by 3 to 6 °C in another, as an estimated 2,000 to 7,000 gigatons of carbon entered the air and ocean. Benthic foraminifera, small seabed animals, suffered a 35 to 50 percent extinction over about 1,000 years, and seawater pH fell by about 0.46 units.

How solid The age is uncertain, the size of the warming is disputed, and the page says acidification may have contributed to the deep-sea extinctions but that temperature, oxygen loss and food supply are also cited. It was not a mass extinction of the scale of the Big Five.

kv.v: Many mammal lineages shrank in size, palms and broadleaf forests spread into the Arctic, and freshwater animals suffered mass deaths from toxic cyanobacterial blooms.
About 200,000 years, 170,000 or 83,000 depending on the method, with an onset under 20,000 years in the helium-3 record.
The page gives peak carbon injection of 0.3 to 1.7 petagrams a year and notes that present emissions exceed 10 gigatons of carbon a year.

items.solid: How solid The age is uncertain, the size of the warming is disputed, and the page says acidification may have contributed to the deep-sea extinctions but that temperature, oxygen loss and food supply are also cited. It was not a mass extinction of the scale of the Big Five.

p: About 65 percent of megafaunal species worldwide became extinct, 72 percent in North America, 83 percent in South America and 88 percent in Australia. All mammals over 1,000 kilograms were lost in Australia and the Americas.
How solid Highly contested on cause. Dating is poor in places, especially North America and the Indian subcontinent, and the page uses both 40 and 45 kilograms as the size threshold.

kv.v: Australia and New Guinea from about 50,000 years ago, northern Eurasia between 50,000 and 10,000, North America around 13,800 to 11,400 years ago, and South America after humans arrived about 15,000 years ago.

Debated between human hunting, climate change and a mix of the two. A 2020 study attributed about 96 percent of mammal extinctions over 126,000 years to humans, covering all mammals, not only megafauna. A 2025 review found the literature remained deeply divided.

items.solid: How solid Highly contested on cause. Dating is poor in places, especially North America and the Indian subcontinent, and the page uses both 40 and 45 kilograms as the size threshold.

p: The species was once the most abundant bird in North America, numbering around 3 billion and possibly up to 5 billion. A slow decline between about 1800 and 1870 became a rapid one between 1870 and 1890.
How solid From Wikipedia. The peak population is an estimate, given as 3 billion and possibly up to 5 billion.

kv.v: The last confirmed wild bird was shot in Indiana in 1902, and the last captive bird, Martha, died at the Cincinnati Zoo on 1 September 1914.
Hunting, which supplied a cheap meat market, together with the loss of the large breeding populations the species needed and widespread deforestation.

items.solid: How solid From Wikipedia. The peak population is an estimate, given as 3 billion and possibly up to 5 billion.

p: The population is put at about 60 million before the 1870s and as low as 541 animals by 1889. The page attributes the fall to commercial hunting and to cattle diseases, and says the killing was part of the genocide of Native Americans, for whom the bison was a central resource.
How solid Weak. The 60 million rests on a single observation from 1871, and the page's own low-point numbers conflict, with 541 in 1889 against 325 in 1884 and 395,000 in 1880.

kv.v: About 31,000 wild bison in 2019 and about 500,000 in total in 2017 including private herds. IUCN counts roughly 15,000 wild, free-range animals, and as few as 12,000 to 15,000 are genetically pure.

items.solid: How solid Weak. The 60 million rests on a single observation from 1871, and the page's own low-point numbers conflict, with 541 in 1889 against 325 in 1884 and 395,000 in 1880.

p: Waves of drought in 1934, 1936 and 1939–1940, combined with deep plowing that removed the native grasses, affected 100 million acres, about 400,000 square kilometres, centred on the Texas and Oklahoma panhandles. More than 500,000 Americans were left homeless, and about 3.5 million people left the Plains states between 1930 and 1940.
How solid From Wikipedia. The topsoil figure is uncited there. The page also notes that regular rainfall returned in fall 1939.

kv.v: In many regions more than 75 percent of the topsoil was blown away by the end of the 1930s, a claim the page marks as needing a citation.

The Soil Erosion Service was created in 1933 and renamed the Soil Conservation Service in 1935. The Civilian Conservation Corps planted a shelterbelt of more than 200 million trees, and by 1938 blowing soil had been reduced by 65 percent.

By 1940 farmland values in high-erosion counties had fallen 28 percent relative to low-erosion counties, and less than a quarter of the original agricultural losses were recovered in the most eroded areas.

items.solid: How solid From Wikipedia. The topsoil figure is uncited there. The page also notes that regular rainfall returned in fall 1939.

p: Soviet cotton irrigation diverted the two rivers that fed the sea. From 1960 to 1998 its surface area fell by 60 percent and its volume by 80 percent, and by 2007 it was about 10 percent of its original size, split into four lakes. The eastern basin of the South Aral dried up completely in August 2014.
How solid From Wikipedia. The page ranks the lake third-largest in one place and fourth-largest in another, and gives the original area as 68,000 square kilometres.

kv.v: Salinity rose from about 10 to about 30 grams a litre by 1990. A fishing industry that employed about 40,000 people and produced a sixth of the Soviet catch ended by 1987, and all native sturgeon species died out.

Kazakhstan finished a dam in 2005 that separated the North Aral. Its level rose 12 metres by 2008, salinity fell to about 8 grams a litre, and almost 24 freshwater species returned. The South Aral remains largely dry.

items.solid: How solid From Wikipedia. The page ranks the lake third-largest in one place and fourth-largest in another, and gives the original area as 68,000 square kilometres.

p: DDT and its breakdown products caused eggshell thinning and population declines in several North American and European birds of prey. Peregrine falcon, bald eagle, osprey and brown pelican eggshells often cracked before hatching, and DDE is considered a major reason for the bald eagle's decline.
How solid From Wikipedia. It gives the causal chain and the dates but no counts, so I cannot say by how much any species fell or recovered.

kv.v: Rachel Carson's Silent Spring appeared in 1962. In summer 1972 the US Environmental Protection Agency cancelled most DDT uses, and a federal appeals court upheld the action in 1973.
The page says the restrictions aided the recovery of endangered species but gives no population figures.

items.solid: How solid From Wikipedia. It gives the causal chain and the dates but no counts, so I cannot say by how much any species fell or recovered.

p: British Antarctic Survey scientists Farman, Gardiner and Shanklin reported the hole in Nature in May 1985. Chlorine from chlorofluorocarbons destroys ozone, and the cold Antarctic spring greatly enhances the process. 43 nations signed the Montreal Protocol in 1987.
How solid From Wikipedia. The page gives the discovery date as both 1982 and 1985. The treaty and its effect are covered in the chapter on nature defended.

kv.v: The seasonal maximum was 21.2 million square kilometres in 2012, and the hole was one of the largest on record at 26 million square kilometres in September 2023.
A 2023 UN assessment projects Antarctic ozone to return to 1980 levels around 2066.

items.solid: How solid From Wikipedia. The page gives the discovery date as both 1982 and 1985. The treaty and its effect are covered in the chapter on nature defended.

p: The epizootic form of the chytrid fungus disease was first discovered in 1993 in dead and dying frogs in Queensland, Australia. A 2019 review in Science linked it to the decline of at least 501 amphibian species over 50 years, 90 of them confirmed or presumed extinct in the wild and 124 down by more than 90 percent.

How solid Contested. A follow-up comment in Science said the 2019 study lacked the evidence for its claims and could not reproduce its conclusions, and the page says it remains unclear how many and which species have been affected.

kv.v: The fungus has been detected in 56 of 82 countries and in 516 of 1,240 species tested, though its presence does not always mean disease.

items.solid: How solid Contested. A follow-up comment in Science said the 2019 study lacked the evidence for its claims and could not reproduce its conclusions, and the page says it remains unclear how many and which species have been affected.

p: The US government estimated that 4.9 million barrels of oil were discharged over 87 days, a figure BP argued was too high. Eleven workers died. Satellite images showed the spill directly affected about 180,000 square kilometres of ocean.
How solid Estimates differ widely and several are disputed by BP. The page gave 19 September as the date the well was sealed; the 20 April start is general knowledge.

kv.v: NOAA estimated between 51,000 and 84,000 killed. Three researchers estimated more than a million coastal birds.
NOAA estimated 56,000 to 166,000 juvenile sea turtles killed, up to a 51 percent decline in the Barataria Bay dolphin population, and 2 to 5 trillion newly hatched fish.

Estimates of the oil that remained ranged from about half to 75 percent, scientists disagreed about the effect of dispersants and about how much microbes broke down the oil, and BP called a 2013 dolphin study inconclusive.

items.solid: How solid Estimates differ widely and several are disputed by BP. The page gave 19 September as the date the well was sealed; the 20 April start is general knowledge.

p: The fires burned more than 24 million hectares, and the state total on 14 January 2020 was 18.6 million hectares. An estimated three billion terrestrial vertebrates, mostly reptiles, were killed or displaced. Some species may have been driven to extinction, with glossy black cockatoos, Kangaroo Island dunnarts and koalas named as being of concern.
How solid The animal figures are estimates that rose sharply, and the page gives no method or confidence range for either. I did not find the page's account of the causes of the fires.

kv.v: 33 direct deaths and 417 indirect deaths from smoke are listed in the infobox, while the state table totals 34 fatalities.
University of Sydney ecologists first estimated 480 million mammals, birds and reptiles lost, a figure later expanded to more than a billion.

items.solid: How solid The animal figures are estimates that rose sharply, and the page gives no method or confidence range for either. I did not find the page's account of the causes of the fires.

patterns.h3: Every deep-time event has an environmental shock behind it
p: The six events before humans each have a change in climate or ocean chemistry among their proposed causes: glaciation, oxygen loss, volcanic carbon dioxide, warming, acidification or an impact winter.

patterns.h3: Recovery takes millions of years
p: After the End-Permian, most marine communities took about 10 million years, land vertebrates about 30 million and global marine diversity about 75 million to regain earlier levels. After the asteroid, forests took about 6 million years.

patterns.h3: In the human era, the pages name human action for most events
p: For seven of the ten events since 50,000 years ago, the pages I read name human action among the causes. The megafauna case is debated, and for the chytrid fungus and the 2019–20 fires the pages gave no cause.

patterns.h3: Four entries record a response after which the measure improved
p: Blowing soil fell 65 percent by 1938 after the Dust Bowl response, DDT uses were cancelled in 1972, the Montreal Protocol was signed in 1987, and the North Aral Sea partly refilled after a dam. In each case the cause was one that could be named and acted on.

patterns.h3: The numbers are soft
p: Estimates for the same event differ widely: Permian marine losses were once put at 90–96 percent, Deepwater Horizon bird deaths at 51,000–84,000 or more than a million, and the bison's starting population rests on one observation.

limits: The list is my selection. Sixteen events cannot cover the record of damage to the living world.
The fossil record is biased by what preserves well, so the deep-time shares are estimates that depend on the method and the taxonomic unit.

Not covered: the other deep-time events such as the end-Capitanian, the Holocene island extinctions such as the dodo and the moa, and other modern cases such as the collapse of the Atlantic cod fishery.
Almost every entry rests on a Wikipedia summary, read through a summarizing tool. They need checking against the original studies before use.
A record kept after the fact covers only what was measured or preserved, so the earlier entries in particular are the ones that left a trace.

p: The framework has 23 global targets, including the aim of protecting at least 30 percent of land and ocean by 2030. By the August 2026 meetings in Nairobi, 172 Parties, almost 90 percent, had submitted national targets, and 130 had submitted national reports. The first global review of progress is due at COP17, 19 to 30 October 2026, in Yerevan.
How solid From the Convention's own press releases. The 2022 adoption date is general knowledge. The review at COP17 had not happened when I wrote this.

kv.v: The Executive Secretary told the Nairobi meeting that fewer than half of aligned national targets assessed by Parties are currently on track.
Mobilizing biodiversity finance, reforming harmful subsidies, addressing business impacts and dependencies, and shifting toward sustainable consumption.

items.solid: How solid From the Convention's own press releases. The 2022 adoption date is general knowledge. The review at COP17 had not happened when I wrote this.

p: The Protected Planet Report 2024 puts coverage at 17.6 percent of land and inland waters and 8.4 percent of ocean and coastal areas. Since 2020, 629,000 square kilometres of land and 1.77 million square kilometres of sea have been added. 51 countries and territories exceed 30 percent on land, and 31 exceed it at sea.
How solid From the report's executive summary, a UN-backed dataset of official submissions. Coverage is counted by area, so it does not show whether protection is enforced.

kv.v: Another 16.7 million square kilometres (12.4 percent) of land and 78.3 million (21.6 percent) of sea.

Only 8.52 percent of land is both protected and connected. Only 5.7 percent of the ocean is in marine protected areas that are implemented or actively managed, and 2.8 percent is fully or highly protected.
Over two-thirds of key biodiversity areas are partially or fully covered, and the remaining 32 percent lie entirely outside protected areas.

items.solid: How solid From the report's executive summary, a UN-backed dataset of official submissions. Coverage is counted by area, so it does not show whether protection is enforced.

p: The Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction passed 60 ratifications on 20 September 2025, with Sierra Leone and Morocco the last two to deposit. It entered into force on 17 January 2026. Palau was the first to ratify, on 22 January 2024.
How solid IUCN's announcement. I found no marine protected area yet created under the treaty, and the page does not give the share of ocean the treaty covers.

kv.v: Marine protected areas beyond national jurisdiction, environmental impact assessments, and rules on access to and benefit sharing from marine genetic resources.

items.solid: How solid IUCN's announcement. I found no marine protected area yet created under the treaty, and the page does not give the share of ocean the treaty covers.

items.h3: Whaling ban and the humpback whale
p: Commercial whaling was curbed and then banned in 1986. Humpbacks in the western South Atlantic fell to a low of 440 in 1958, from about 27,000 before hunting. A 2019 study estimates about 25,000 now, roughly 93 percent of the pre-hunt level.
How solid One population of one species, reported by Science News. Other whale populations recovered less, and the ban is only one factor.

kv.v: Zerbini and colleagues, Royal Society Open Science, published online 16 October 2019.

items.solid: How solid One population of one species, reported by Science News. Other whale populations recovered less, and the ban is only one factor.

p: Bolam and colleagues estimate that conservation action prevented at least 28 bird and mammal extinctions since 1993: 21 to 32 birds and 7 to 16 mammals. They drew on 137 experts.
How solid The figures are estimates of what would have happened without conservation, not counts. The study covers birds and mammals only.

kv.v: In the same period 15 bird and mammal species went extinct or are strongly suspected to have done so. The vaquita is still declining quickly.

items.solid: How solid The figures are estimates of what would have happened without conservation, not counts. The study covers birds and mammals only.

p: Brazil's DETER system recorded 2,874.38 square kilometres of deforestation alerts from August 2025 to July 2026, down from 4,495 in the previous period. That is the lowest since the series began in 2016 and 55.6 percent below the average of the last ten cycles.

How solid A report in Agência Brasil of figures from the national space research institute. The article says the fall was 36.87 percent, but the two areas it gives imply about 36.06 percent, and it does not explain the gap. Alerts are not the same as the annual official count.
items.solid: How solid A report in Agência Brasil of figures from the national space research institute. The article says the fall was 36.87 percent, but the two areas it gives imply about 36.06 percent, and it does not explain the gap. Alerts are not the same as the annual official count.

p: The law took effect on 18 August 2024. Member States must have restoration measures in place on at least 20 percent of the EU's land and 20 percent of its sea by 2030, and for all ecosystems that need restoration by 2050.
How solid From the European Commission's announcement. I did not check whether Member States met the 2026 deadline for draft plans.

kv.v: Draft national restoration plans are due two years after entry into force, so about August 2026, with reviews by 2032 and 2042.
The law aims to restore at least 25,000 kilometres of rivers by 2030.

items.solid: How solid From the European Commission's announcement. I did not check whether Member States met the 2026 deadline for draft plans.

items.h3: Ozone layer and the Montreal Protocol
p: The phase-out covers nearly 99 percent of banned ozone-depleting substances. If current policies stay, the ozone layer is expected to return to 1980 levels by about 2066 over the Antarctic, 2045 over the Arctic and 2040 elsewhere. In the 2026 Planetary Health Check, stratospheric ozone is one of two boundaries that are not transgressed.
How solid The WMO page and a summary of the 2026 check. The 1987 date is general knowledge. Ozone and aerosols are the two boundaries that have improved over the last decade.
items.solid: How solid The WMO page and a summary of the 2026 check. The 1987 date is general knowledge. Ozone and aerosols are the two boundaries that have improved over the last decade.

p: Wild catch has stayed in a band of 86 to 94 million tonnes since the late 1980s, about 92 million tonnes in 2024, while farmed aquatic animal production passed 100 million tonnes. 62.4 percent of assessed stocks are fished sustainably.
How solid FAO's 2026 report through Mongabay. A steady catch can reflect management or limits on stocks, and the report's stock count changed from about 500 to 2,665 between editions.

kv.v: The sustainable share fell 2.1 points from the 2024 report.

items.solid: How solid FAO's 2026 report through Mongabay. A steady catch can reflect management or limits on stocks, and the report's stock count changed from about 500 to 2,665 between editions.

p: At the International Seabed Authority's two-week Council session reported on 20 March 2026, no mining was approved. The Mining Code, the rulebook needed before commercial extraction, remains unfinished. 40 countries back a moratorium.
How solid A report in Oceanographic Magazine. I did not find the outcome of the July meeting, so this describes the position in March.

kv.v: Concern about unilateral mining outside the Authority, centred on a Nauru-linked subsidiary of The Metals Company. A report on it was due at the July meeting.

items.solid: How solid A report in Oceanographic Magazine. I did not find the outcome of the July meeting, so this describes the position in March.

p: International finance to developing countries was $29.8 billion in 2023 for biodiversity-related spending and $16.8 billion for biodiversity-specific spending, against a target of $20 billion a year by 2025. The 2030 target is $30 billion a year.
How solid From a UK government finance dashboard. The page gives no current total for the $200 billion target or for subsidies, so I cannot say how close either is.

kv.v: $200 billion a year from all sources by 2030, and $500 billion of harmful subsidies reduced or reformed.
A $700 billion annual biodiversity funding gap by 2030.
$220 billion of total annual flows in 2023, up 11 percent on 2022, of which $23.4 billion was private.

items.solid: How solid From a UK government finance dashboard. The page gives no current total for the $200 billion target or for subsidies, so I cannot say how close either is.

patterns.h3: Defenses work best on a single, countable cause
p: The whaling ban, the ozone chemicals and the Amazon alerts each target one act that can be monitored. The recoveries in this chapter are of that kind.

patterns.h3: Targets are ahead of delivery
p: The 30 percent targets stand against 17.6 and 8.4 percent coverage and much smaller shares that are managed or strictly protected.

patterns.h3: Diffuse drivers have no comparable instrument
p: Land-use change, consumption, plastic and ocean heat are spread across many actors. For these the entries describe frameworks and negotiations, and I found no measured turnaround.

patterns.h3: Recovery is slow and species-specific
p: The humpback population reached about 93 percent of its pre-hunt size roughly 33 years after the ban, and the same studies show other species still falling. Conservation prevented at least 28 extinctions while 15 others occurred.

limits: The list is my selection. Eleven entries cannot cover the many local and national defenses, and I did not cover freshwater protection, soil, invasive species control or national endangered species laws.
Cause is hard to show. A rise in a population or fall in deforestation may reflect enforcement, prices, weather or all three, and the sources say so in only some cases.
Several items are early. The framework's global review, the July seabed meeting and the national restoration plans were still pending or unchecked when I wrote this.
Coverage counts area, not outcome. A protected area that is not managed is counted in the 17.6 and 8.4 percent.
Most figures reached me through summaries, so they need checking against the original reports before use.

items.h3: From the farm to other work
p: Around one-quarter of the world's labour force works in agriculture. In many low- and middle-income countries the majority works in farming and relies on it as its main income, as most people did in rich countries a few centuries ago. As countries get richer the share working in agriculture tends to fall as people move into industry and services.
How solid The page gives the one-quarter figure and these statements, but its history is in charts whose data the text does not include. I have no figure for the share in agriculture in 1825 or 1925.

kv.v: Value added per farm worker can differ ten-fold between countries.

items.solid: How solid The page gives the one-quarter figure and these statements, but its history is in charts whose data the text does not include. I have no figure for the share in agriculture in 1825 or 1925.

p: The ILO and UNICEF estimate nearly 138 million children were in child labour in 2024, down from 246 million in 2000, with about 54 million in hazardous work. Agriculture accounts for 61%, services 27% and industry 13%. Sub-Saharan Africa has about 87 million, nearly two-thirds of the total, while in Asia and the Pacific prevalence fell from 6% to 3% since 2020.

How solid The 2024 and 2000 figures are from the ILO and UNICEF release. Our World in Data gives 265 million in 2013 from an earlier ILO report, and the two reports may not use the same method, so I do not draw a straight line through them.

kv.v: Child work was widespread in 19th-century Europe and North America and fell rapidly around the turn of the 20th century. Our World in Data says England's 1900 child labour rate was similar to today's global rate. Among 12 to 14 year olds in England and Wales it fell to about 6–7% after the First World War and rose to 15.3% by 1944.
The release warns that global funding cuts threaten to roll back the gains.

items.solid: How solid The 2024 and 2000 figures are from the ILO and UNICEF release. Our World in Data gives 265 million in 2013 from an earlier ILO report, and the two reports may not use the same method, so I do not draw a straight line through them.

p: Around half of women worldwide take part in the labour force, a figure ILO estimates say has stayed around 50% since the early 1990s, while men's participation fell from 80% in 1990 to around 73%. In 2024 it was 62% in Sweden, 56% in Germany and 41% in Italy.
How solid From Our World in Data's page on the ILO's modelled estimates. The page gives no regional percentages and no US participation figures for 1900 or 1950.

kv.v: Women spend more time on unpaid care than men in every country, in some by more than six times. Average US household housework fell from 58 hours a week in 1900 to 18 in 1975.

items.solid: How solid From Our World in Data's page on the ILO's modelled estimates. The page gives no regional percentages and no US participation figures for 1900 or 1950.

p: An ILO analysis reported on 12 May 2026 found nearly 58% of workers globally in informal jobs.
How solid Thin. It is a news report of an ILO analysis, with no worker count, no regions and no definition, and I did not read the ILO's own page.
items.solid: How solid Thin. It is a news report of an ILO analysis, with no worker count, no regions and no definition, and I did not read the ILO's own page.

items.h3: How much depends on where you live
p: Milanovic (2015) is cited as finding that the country a person lives in explains two-thirds of the variation of income differences among all people. The poorer half of the world, almost 4 billion people, live on less than $6.70 a day, and someone on $30 a day is in the richest 15%. Swedes are about 30 times richer than in 1820, and about 96% of the world's people live in the country they were born in.
How solid From Our World in Data's introduction to global inequality. The page gives no Gini or Theil values and no top-10% shares, so I cannot show how total inequality moved over two centuries.

kv.v: The figures use 2011 international dollars from an earlier World Bank release, and the page notes the World Bank has since updated its data.

items.solid: How solid From Our World in Data's introduction to global inequality. The page gives no Gini or Theil values and no top-10% shares, so I cannot show how total inequality moved over two centuries.

p: The World Inequality Report 2026, as reported, says the richest 10% earn 53% of global income and the poorer half of adults, about 2.8 billion, 8%. The richest 10% own 75% of global wealth, the richest 1% own 37% and the poorer half 2%. Around 56,000 people, the top 0.001%, hold more wealth than 2.8 billion adults together.
How solid From a news report of the report, not the report. It gives no earlier shares, so it shows how things stand and not whether they have changed.

kv.v: Average wealth in North America and Oceania in 2025 is more than sixteen times that of Sub-Saharan Africa.

items.solid: How solid From a news report of the report, not the report. It gives no earlier shares, so it shows how things stand and not whether they have changed.

p: Population growth peaked in the 1960s at over 2% a year, 2.3% in 1963 on the chart, and was 0.9% in 2023. The UN projects a peak of about 10.3 billion in the mid-2080s and about 10.2 billion by 2100, from 8.2 billion in 2024. 63 countries have already passed their peak, including China, Germany, Japan and Russia. The number of children under five peaked in 2017.
How solid These are projections and the page says they are sensitive to assumptions about fertility.

kv.v: Our World in Data's text says the peak is in 2086 at just over 10.4 billion, while a chart on the same page says about 10.3 billion in 2084, and the two seem to come from different UN editions.

items.solid: How solid These are projections and the page says they are sensitive to assumptions about fertility.

p: The world's fertility rate was 4.9 in the 1950s and 2.3 in 2023. Niger had 6 in 2023. South Korea fell from around 6 in the 1950s to less than 1, and most countries in East Asia were below 1. India fell from about 5 in the 1970s to about 2. More than half of all countries are below the replacement level of 2.1, and nearly a fifth have fewer than 1.4.
How solid Our World in Data and the UN, read through a summarizing tool. The UN page gave no world fertility rate for 2024 and none for 1950 itself, so the 1950s figure is Our World in Data's.
items.solid: How solid Our World in Data and the UN, read through a summarizing tool. The UN page gave no world fertility rate for 2024 and none for 1950 itself, so the 1950s figure is Our World in Data's.

p: The UN expects people aged 65 or over to outnumber children under 18 by the late 2070s. Global life expectancy was 73.3 in 2024, up from 70.9 in the pandemic.

How solid A projection. The page gave no share of the population aged 65 or over today, and its pandemic life expectancy of 70.9 differs from the 71.5 that WHO gives in Chapter 3, and I did not check why.
items.solid: How solid A projection. The page gave no share of the population aged 65 or over today, and its pandemic life expectancy of 70.9 differs from the 71.5 that WHO gives in Chapter 3, and I did not check why.

p: Around one in four people in urban areas live in slum households, and in sub-Saharan Africa more than half of urban residents do, with Chad near 80%.
How solid From Our World in Data's page on urbanization. It gives no total count of people living in slums and no year for the shares.

kv.v: Chapter 1 gives the rise in the share of people living in cities.

items.solid: How solid From Our World in Data's page on urbanization. It gives no total count of people living in slums and no year for the shares.

patterns.h3: Where people live now matters more than much else
p: The country of residence explains two-thirds of income differences, 96% of people live where they were born, and child labour, informal work, slum living and low internet access all concentrate in the poorer regions, on the figures in this and the earlier chapters.

patterns.h3: Child labour has fallen by almost half in 24 years and is still large
p: From 246 million in 2000 to 138 million in 2024 is a fall of 44%, on my division, and the ILO release says funding cuts could reverse it.

patterns.h3: The turn in population is already here for many countries
p: More than half of countries are below replacement fertility and 63 have passed their peak, while the world total is projected to keep rising until the 2080s.

patterns.h3: Shares of income and wealth are given for one year only
p: The 2025 figures show the shape of inequality but not its history, so this chapter cannot say whether inequality rose or fell across the century.

patterns.h3: The data do not fall on 1825 and 1925
p: Child labour starts in 2000, fertility in the 1950s, inequality shares in 2025. A comparison of the two centuries cannot be made on these figures.

items.h3: Scores on intelligence tests rose for decades
p: In the United States average scores on the Wechsler scales rose by about three IQ points a decade, and Trahan and colleagues put it at 2.93 a decade in 2014. Dutch conscripts gained 21 points over 30 years, 1952 to 1982, and British children on Raven's Progressive Matrices gained 14 points from 1942 to 2008. Gains were continuous and roughly linear from the earliest testing to the mid-1990s.
How solid From Wikipedia's article on the Flynn effect, which cites the studies. Gains were concentrated at the lower end in some studies, and the sizes differ between tests and countries.

kv.v: Schooling, at 1 to 5 points for each extra year, nutrition, falling lead exposure, less infectious disease and a more visual, abstract environment. No single cause is agreed.
Whether intelligence itself has risen is still controversial, the gains may reflect test-specific skills, and school-content subtests such as vocabulary and arithmetic changed little.

items.solid: How solid From Wikipedia's article on the Flynn effect, which cites the studies. Gains were concentrated at the lower end in some studies, and the sizes differ between tests and countries.

p: About 1 in 10 people could read and write in 1820, and about 88% of adults and 93% of 15 to 24 year olds can now, on UNESCO figures as reported. Chapter 5 gives the series, the definitions and the 739 million adults who still lack basic literacy.
How solid Repeats Chapter 5, where the early figures are described as soft and the UNESCO figures come from a news report.
items.solid: How solid Repeats Chapter 5, where the early figures are described as soft and the UNESCO figures come from a news report.

items.h3: In several rich countries the rise stopped, then fell
p: In Norway gains in general intelligence among conscripts stopped after the mid-1990s and numerical reasoning declined. Bratsberg and Rogeberg found that for men born 1962 to 1991 the rise, its turning point and the decline all appear within families, and they found no support for explanations based on genes or on factors that differ between families. In Denmark conscripts gained about 3 points a decade from 1959 to 1979 and about 1.3 from 1989 to 1998, then lost about as much between 1998 and 2004. In the UK the average 14 year old's score fell by more than two points between 1980 and 2008.
How solid Norway's data cover only men, with women's scores approximated from years of schooling. The page gives no figures for Finland or France and the reversals are for specific tests and cohorts.

kv.v: Winter and colleagues found gains of about 1.2 points a decade in a 2024 comparison, rather than the 3 expected. Gonthier and colleagues argue there is no negative Flynn effect in France, and that tests based on cultural knowledge can misstate variation.
No rise in the scores of 6 to 12 year olds from 1975 to 2003.

items.solid: How solid Norway's data cover only men, with women's scores approximated from years of schooling. The page gives no figures for Finland or France and the reversals are for specific tests and cohorts.

p: The average international score in mathematics fell by 15 points between 2018 and 2022, about three-quarters of a year of learning, and reading fell by about half a year. Science stayed about the same. The survey covered 81 countries and regions, and Germany, Iceland and the Netherlands each fell by 25 points or more in mathematics. Singapore ranked first.
How solid From a news report of the OECD's results. It gives no point figure for reading and does not say whether the average is for the OECD alone.

kv.v: School closures in the pandemic are likely part of it, but the OECD said it is not just about Covid and that long-term issues in education systems are also to blame. The report does not say how much belongs to each.

items.solid: How solid From a news report of the OECD's results. It gives no point figure for reading and does not say whether the average is for the OECD alone.

p: The OECD's second Survey of Adult Skills covered 31 countries and about 160,000 adults aged 16 to 65, with 27 countries also in the first survey. Only Finland and Denmark improved significantly in literacy, and most other countries declined or stayed flat. The lowest 10% fell in most countries while the top 10% rose. About one in five adults can only understand simple texts or do basic arithmetic.
How solid From a news summary of the OECD's press release. I could not read the press release itself, and the summary gives no exact count of countries that declined.

kv.v: Declines were larger among low-educated adults. In some places a rising share of foreign-born adults, who score lower, explains part of the fall. Men's literacy fell more than women's.
Eight countries raised their averages, Finland and Singapore the most.

items.solid: How solid From a news summary of the OECD's press release. I could not read the press release itself, and the summary gives no exact count of countries that declined.

p: A study of the American Time Use Survey, over 236,000 Americans, found the share reading for pleasure on a given day fell by more than 40% over 20 years, a steady decline of about 3% a year. It was published in iScience in August 2025.
How solid A university's news release of the study. It gives no starting level and covers the United States only.
items.solid: How solid A university's news release of the study. It gives no starting level and covers the United States only.

items.h3: Children who cannot read a simple text
p: The World Bank and UNICEF estimated in June 2022 that 70% of 10-year-olds in low- and middle-income countries could not read and understand a simple text, up from 57% before the pandemic. The rate was 89% in sub-Saharan Africa, and was predicted to rise from about 50% to 80% in Latin America and the Caribbean and from 60% to 78% in South Asia.
How solid A UNICEF press release of the estimate. Parts are predictions for the pandemic's effect, and the pre-pandemic figure is a revised one against an earlier estimate of 53% for 2015.

kv.v: Learning poverty is the share of 10-year-olds who cannot read and understand a simple text.

items.solid: How solid A UNICEF press release of the estimate. Parts are predictions for the pandemic's effect, and the pre-pandemic figure is a revised one against an earlier estimate of 53% for 2015.

p: There is no scientific consensus on the definition of wisdom. Baltes's Berlin Wisdom Paradigm describes five components, among them factual and procedural knowledge of life matters and an apprehension of uncertainty. Sternberg's balance theory calls it the value-laden application of tacit knowledge to attain a common good. It is measured by self-report scales, which are prone to bias, by indices such as the Jeste-Thomas Wisdom Index, and by contextual measures of cognition, motivation and emotion in specific situations.
How solid From Wikipedia. The page itself says the usefulness of the shortest scales is increasingly questioned.

kv.v: I found no series that tracks wisdom over a century or even a decade.

items.solid: How solid From Wikipedia. The page itself says the usefulness of the shortest scales is increasingly questioned.

patterns.h3: The evidence points both ways, by measure
p: Test scores rose for most of the 20th century and the reading rate rose from 1 in 10 to 88%. Several recent measures fell: the Flynn gains reversed in some countries, PISA mathematics dropped, adult literacy fell or stayed flat in most surveyed countries and reading for pleasure fell in the United States.

patterns.h3: Where the evidence falls, it does not fall everywhere
p: Finland and Denmark improved in adult literacy, Finland and Singapore in numeracy, Singapore led PISA 2022, and the top 10% of adults gained while the lowest 10% fell. The picture is one of widening gaps in some places, not a uniform decline.

patterns.h3: Access and ability are separate things
p: Chapter 5 shows access to schooling and the internet rising, yet 70% of 10-year-olds in low- and middle-income countries could not read a simple text in 2022 and about 1 in 5 adults in the surveyed countries read only simple texts.

patterns.h3: The question asks about wisdom, which cannot be measured
p: No agreed definition or series exists, so 'dumbed down' can be tested only on the narrower measures of tests, skills and reading, and they give a mixed answer.

patterns.h3: The data do not reach back to 1925 on most measures
p: The Flynn series start in the 1940s and 1950s, the literacy series in 1820, PISA in 2018 and the adult skills survey in 2012, so the two centuries cannot be compared.

limits: Wisdom, judgement and the use of knowledge have no accepted measure, and nothing here tracks them over time.
Test scores measure particular skills at particular dates. Tests change, and so do the people who take them, including through migration.
Most of the reversal evidence is from a few rich countries, and most of the learning evidence for poorer countries is from one estimate.
Several figures are news reports of reports and of studies. I could not read the OECD adult skills press release or the PNAS article and used a summary of each.
Not covered: critical thinking, belief in misinformation, civic knowledge, the effect of search engines and artificial intelligence, and how people judge what they read.
The chapter weighs evidence on one side and the other and does not reach a verdict on the question.

items.h3: How many people live with a mental disorder
p: WHO's fact sheet says nearly 1 in 7 people, 1.2 billion, were living with a mental disorder in 2023. That included 470 million with anxiety disorders, 146 million of them children and adolescents, and 322 million with depression, 43 million of them children and adolescents. Among adolescents aged 10 to 19 it counts 3.3 million with bipolar disorder, 4.7 million with eating disorders and 39 million with conduct-dissocial disorder.
How solid The WHO figures are modelled estimates. The pages give no earlier figures, so they show scale and not change.

kv.v: WHO's 2025 reports describe anxiety and depression as the second leading cause of long-term disability, with over 1 billion people living with mental health conditions.
Our World in Data cites an estimate, with no year, that 1 in 3 women and 1 in 5 men will experience major depression in their lives.

items.solid: How solid The WHO figures are modelled estimates. The pages give no earlier figures, so they show scale and not change.

p: Most people with mental disorders do not have access to effective care. Only 40% of people with psychosis and one third of people with depression receive formal mental health care. The median government spends just 2% of its total health budget on mental health, according to a September 2025 WHO release citing the Mental Health Atlas 2024. For drug use disorders, the UN report says only about one in five people with serious disorders receive treatment.
How solid WHO's own pages, plus a news report for the drug figure. The release gave no reference year for the spending figure.

kv.v: WHO describes stark disparities between high- and low-income countries and a shortage of workforce, but the pages I read give no figures.

items.solid: How solid WHO's own pages, plus a news report for the drug figure. The release gave no reference year for the spending figure.

p: WHO says 727,000 people take their own life each year, though the same page elsewhere says more than 720,000. In 2021, 73% of suicides, close to three quarters, were in low- and middle-income countries, and suicide was the third leading cause of death among 15 to 29 year olds. WHO says many people are not seeking help and so are not getting the help they need.
How solid The page gives no year for the 727,000, no rate per 100,000 and no trend. I did not find a long-run series.

kv.v: If this subject is close to you, speaking to a doctor, a trusted person or a local crisis line is a sensible step.

items.solid: How solid The page gives no year for the 727,000, no rate per 100,000 and no trend. I did not find a long-run series.

p: The 2025 World Drug Report, as reported, says more than 316 million people used drugs in 2023, 6% of adults aged 15 to 65, up from 5.2% in 2013. About 63 million people had drug use disorders in 2022, and there were about 25 million cocaine users. Fentanyl caused more than 100,000 deaths in the United States in 2023.
How solid A news report of a UN report. I did not read the report, and I found no figure for drug use before 2013.
items.solid: How solid A news report of a UN report. I did not read the report, and I found no figure for drug use before 2013.

p: WHO's Commission on Social Connection says 1 in 6 people worldwide is affected by loneliness, linked to more than 871,000 deaths a year, about 100 an hour. Between 17% and 21% of people aged 13 to 29 report loneliness, highest among teenagers. About 24% of people in low-income countries report it, about double the 11% in high-income countries.
How solid From WHO's own news release. How the 871,000 deaths were attributed is not stated on the page.

kv.v: Social isolation is estimated to affect up to 1 in 3 older adults and 1 in 4 adolescents, though data on older adults are limited.

items.solid: How solid From WHO's own news release. How the 871,000 deaths were attributed is not stated on the page.

items.h3: How satisfied people say they are
p: In the World Happiness Report 2026 Finland ranked first for a record ninth year, Costa Rica fourth, its highest ranking, and Switzerland tenth. Our World in Data says countries with higher average incomes tend to report higher life satisfaction, and that the share saying they are very or rather happy rose in most countries with two or more surveys. In Albania it went from 33.4% in 1998 to 73.9% in 2022, while in Greece satisfaction fell from about 67% in 2007 to 32.4% five years later.

How solid The report page gives rankings but no global average, scale or data years, and I did not read the full report. The trend figures are from two survey series that do not cover the whole world.

kv.v: Life satisfaction is the Gallup World Poll's 0 to 10 ladder, from the worst to the best possible life, asked in more than 160 countries.

items.solid: How solid The report page gives rankings but no global average, scale or data years, and I did not read the full report. The trend figures are from two survey series that do not cover the whole world.

items.h3: Screens and the well-being of the young
p: The World Happiness Report 2026 says heavy social media use appears to be contributing to the drop in well-being among young people in English-speaking countries and Western Europe, especially among girls. WHO's report on social connection also calls for attention to excessive screen time and negative online interactions.
How solid Tentative. The wording is 'appears to be', so it is an observed association and not a proven cause, and it is limited to some regions.
items.solid: How solid Tentative. The wording is 'appears to be', so it is an observed association and not a proven cause, and it is limited to some regions.

patterns.h3: The scale is large and the care is thin
p: More than 1 in 7 people live with a mental disorder, and for depression only one third receive formal care while governments spend a median 2% of health budgets on mental health.

patterns.h3: The record cannot say whether mental illness has become more common
p: None of the pages I read gives a long-run series of prevalence, and Our World in Data says many people do not report symptoms, which makes prevalence hard to estimate. The 1925 comparison cannot be made on these figures.

patterns.h3: Life satisfaction goes with income and is hit by crises
p: Across countries higher average income goes with higher satisfaction, it rose in most countries with repeated surveys, and Greece fell sharply after the financial crisis. These are patterns in two survey series, not a cause.

patterns.h3: The young are a focus of the 2025 and 2026 reports
p: WHO and the World Happiness Report both single out young people, for loneliness and for the possible effect of screens, and both are cautious about cause.

patterns.h3: Loneliness and care both differ by income
p: Loneliness is reported about twice as often in low-income countries as in high-income ones, and WHO describes stark gaps in care between them, though the pages give no figures for the care gap.

limits: Mental health is measured here by modelled counts, surveys and self-reports, and many people do not report symptoms.
I found no long-run series on mental disorders, suicide, loneliness or life satisfaction, so this chapter cannot compare the century before 1925 with the century after.
Several figures are news reports of reports: the World Drug Report and the Happiness Report rankings were not read in full.
Life satisfaction is a self-rating on a 0 to 10 ladder, and cultures answer such questions differently.
Not covered: sleep, stress at work, dementia, grief, the effect of war and violence, and the experience of people with severe illness.
A count of deaths by suicide says nothing about why individuals take their own lives, and I found no rate per 100,000 or share of the poorer countries' population to set the 73% against.

items.h3: From closed autocracy to electoral democracy and back
p: Our World in Data, using the Regimes of the World classification, says almost everyone in 1800 lived under closed autocracies, with about 20 million people in electoral autocracies, which it names as the UK and US. Electoral and liberal democracy spread widely in the 20th century, especially in its second half. The world was at its democratic all-time high in the early 2010s and has fallen since. By 2025 about 1.6 billion people lived in electoral democracies and another 600 million in liberal democracies.

How solid One classification among several, which the page says sometimes sort countries differently. It gives no share of the world's people in 1900 or 1950, and no count of countries by regime for 2025.

kv.v: The page says population growth outpaced democratic expansion, so the number of people without democratic rights is higher than ever, with many in China.
RoW reclassified India as an electoral autocracy in 2017, while other sources agree it has become less democratic but still count it as a democracy.

items.solid: How solid One classification among several, which the page says sometimes sort countries differently. It gives no share of the world's people in 1900 or 1950, and no count of countries by regime for 2025.

p: The V-Dem Institute's 2026 report, as reported, says democracy for the average person has fallen back to the level of 1978. Of 179 countries, 87 are democracies, 31 of them liberal and 56 electoral, and 92 are autocracies, 57 electoral and 35 closed. An estimated 74% of the world's people, about 6 billion, live in autocracies and 26% in democracies. 44 countries, with 41% of the world's population, are autocratizing, and 18, with 5%, are democratizing.
How solid A news report of V-Dem's report, covering developments through 2025. I did not read the report, and V-Dem's method differs from the Regimes of the World classification above.
items.solid: How solid A news report of V-Dem's report, covering developments through 2025. I did not read the report, and V-Dem's method differs from the Regimes of the World classification above.

p: Freedom House's Freedom in the World 2026 report says global freedom declined for the 20th consecutive year in 2025. 54 countries saw their political rights and civil liberties deteriorate and only 35 improved. 88 countries are rated Free.
How solid From Freedom House's own press release. It gave no current count of Partly Free and Not Free countries.
items.solid: How solid From Freedom House's own press release. It gave no current count of Partly Free and Not Free countries.

p: New Zealand granted women the national vote first, in 1893. The United States did so in 1920, Britain in 1918 for some women and in 1928 on the same terms as men, India in 1921 in two provinces and 1929 in all provinces, and France in 1944. Women could vote at the federal level in Switzerland from 1971 and in Saudi Arabia's local elections from 2015.
How solid From Wikipedia. The dates are for the vote, which in several places was partial or limited by race, region or class. The page gives no count of countries with women's suffrage in any year.

kv.v: The page lists Vatican City and Eritrea as having no voting, and notes that some countries have suspended national elections.

items.solid: How solid From Wikipedia. The dates are for the vote, which in several places was partial or limited by race, region or class. The page gives no count of countries with women's suffrage in any year.

p: Reporters Without Borders says the average score of all countries assessed in its 2026 index has never been so low in 25 years. 52.2% of countries and territories are rated difficult or very serious, against 13.7% in 2002, and less than 1% of the world's population lives in a country rated good.
How solid From RSF's own page. It gives no global average score and no count of countries in each category, and I did not use its journalist-casualty figures.

kv.v: 52.2% of 180 is about 94 countries, my calculation.

items.solid: How solid From RSF's own page. It gives no global average score and no count of countries in each category, and I did not use its journalist-casualty figures.

p: Transparency International's 2025 index, scored from 0 to 100 with lower meaning more perceived public-sector corruption, gives a global average of 42, the lowest in a decade. 122 of 182 countries score below 50. Denmark is first with 89 for the eighth year, and Somalia and South Sudan share last place with 9. 50 countries have declined since 2012.

How solid A law-firm summary of the index. The index measures perceptions of corruption, not corruption itself, and the summary's statement of an 8-point drop in the average looks wrong, so I left it out.

kv.v: Declining examples include the US at 64, Canada at 75 and France at 66, while Estonia (76), South Korea (63) and Bhutan (71) are cited as consistent improvers.

items.solid: How solid A law-firm summary of the index. The index measures perceptions of corruption, not corruption itself, and the summary's statement of an 8-point drop in the average looks wrong, so I left it out.

p: The United Nations now lists 193 member states, the most recent being South Sudan, admitted on 14 July 2011.
How solid Thin. The page gives the count and the latest member only, and I found no figure for the number of independent states in 1825 or 1925.
